text:
Sam: Kicking off blue->green shift in 10m for release v2.9.0. Change window 23:00-01:00 PT. Plan: 5% increments every 3m, pause on p95>200ms or errors>0.5%. I’ll post live updates.
ReleaseBot: Deploy pipeline triggered: canary to pool-east-2 started (job: deploy/v2.9.0/canary). Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/blue-green-shift. Auto-alerts enabled.
Jess: Quick question — are we pinning router binary to 2.3.1 during the shift to avoid header churn?
Mohit: Yes, orchestrator already pinned router=2.3.1 for this change. LB config was validated in staging.
Sam: Ops checklist snippet for weights (for on-call):
```
# set green weight to x% (via router admin)
curl -X POST "https://router-admin.internal/weights" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"green": 15, "blue": 85}'
# verify
curl "https://router-admin.internal/status" | jq .routes.myservice
```
deploy-bot: Applied weight update: green=5 -> green=10 (step 2). Observability links: p95/p50/dash: https://grafana/team/releases/v2.9.0
Morgan: Watching latency and errors. p50 stable, p95 creeping: 185ms at 10% green. No spike in 5xx yet.
Sam: Continue. Remember to tag the release notes: add rollback rationale and canary metrics to the changelog.
deploy-bot: Applied weight update: green=15 (step 3).
Morgan: Alert: error-rate at 15% green = 0.62% (threshold 0.5%). Pausing rollout.
Sam: Paused. Good call. Decision needed: immediate rollback to blue or drill down while holding at 15%?
Jess: If errors are traffic-correlated and climbing, prefer full rollback. Any trace sampling?
Mohit: Traces show increased timeout errors from connector-x on green instances. Looks like a dependency regression in v2.9.0.
Sam: Rollback decision: set green weight back to 0 and mark release v2.9.0 as failed. Execute rollback plan.
deploy-bot: Executing rollback: setting green=0 -> blue=100. Confirming service health.
ReleaseBot: Rollback complete. Canary terminated. Incident stub created: INC-7891. Please fill in root cause in the postmortem doc.
Morgan: Monitoring after rollback: p95 back to 140ms, errors down to 0.08%.
Jess: Tagging this in release notes: "v2.9.0 rollout paused and rolled back due to connector-x timeouts; pinning policy kept routers compatible; working on dependency fix."
Sam: Thanks team. Next steps: dev to fix connector regression, new canary after patch. I’ll schedule a narrow change window for reattempt. :thumbsup:
